newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SK Telecom buys 20 pct stake in Thai firm.
newsitem.headline: SK Telecom buys 20 pct stake in Thai firm.

text.p: South Korea's SK Telecom bought a 20 percent stake in Wireless Communications Services of Thailand for $150 million, a company spokesman said on Friday.
The spokesman said the South Korean company had become the second largest shareholder in the Thai mobile phone service provider.
M Group and its affiliates hold a combined 48 percent stake in Wireless Communications, which is due to provide a new DCS-1800 digital cellular service this month.
SK Telecom will participate in managing the Thai company by sending two directors. The company is also planning to transfer its know-how on radio frequency engineering and operations.
The spokesman said SK Telecom needed to develop new markets as competition was increasing in South Korea. The South Korean telecommunications market will be fully liberalised next year.
He forecast the number of mobile service users in Thailand would grow to five million by the year 2000. Users totalled 1.8 million last year in a population of 60 million.
